regions.name: input
regions.note: the problem's own stream: `0 addr` (READ) / `1 addr value` (WRITE)

regions.name: head
regions.note: the only room that talks to I/O. Swaps the stream's `op addr` into the tree's `addr op [value]`, and on a READ waits for the answer before starting the next operation — that serialisation is what keeps answers ordered when latency down the tree differs per address. Ports: input and answer arrive on the north wall (over interior cols 1 and 8), the command leaves the south wall under col 5, the answer leaves east on row 1.

regions.name: output
regions.note: one word per READ, in stream order

regions.name: mid router
regions.note: one `/` splits the address: quotient (the block, 0..3) drives BP, remainder (the local address, 0..3) is relayed on. Then a single walk east: `d` bypasses a lane while BP>0 and peels into it at BP==0, so lane j owns addresses j*4..j*4+3.

regions.name: mid lane 0 -> addr 0..3
regions.note: BP==0 peels here; the command pipe leaves the south wall under this lane's `v` and runs to the leaf router 3 blocks down (lane j feeds block k1-1-j, which is what keeps the fan-out planar).

regions.name: mid lane 1 -> addr 4..7
regions.note: BP==1 peels here; the command pipe leaves the south wall under this lane's `v` and runs to the leaf router 2 blocks down (lane j feeds block k1-1-j, which is what keeps the fan-out planar).

regions.name: mid lane 2 -> addr 8..11
regions.note: BP==2 peels here; the command pipe leaves the south wall under this lane's `v` and runs to the leaf router 1 blocks down (lane j feeds block k1-1-j, which is what keeps the fan-out planar).

regions.name: mid lane 3 -> addr 12..15
regions.note: BP==3 peels here; the command pipe leaves the south wall under this lane's `v` and runs to the leaf router 0 blocks down (lane j feeds block k1-1-j, which is what keeps the fan-out planar).

regions.name: leaf router block 3 (addr 12..15)
regions.note: `>rb` loads BP = the local address, then the same walk east: lane i peels to the cell holding addr 12+i. Fed by mid lane 3; every `r` in here (including the WRITE value at the far end of the lane) binds to that one incoming pipe, which is why the packet needs no dummy tokens.

regions.name: cell addr 12
regions.note: address 12 = mid lane 3 * 4 + leaf lane 0. The resident man's B *is* the stored value — 0 until the first WRITE, so there is no initialisation pass. READ 12 ticks, WRITE 8.

regions.name: cell addr 13
regions.note: address 13 = mid lane 3 * 4 + leaf lane 1. The resident man's B *is* the stored value — 0 until the first WRITE, so there is no initialisation pass. READ 12 ticks, WRITE 8.

regions.name: cell addr 14
regions.note: address 14 = mid lane 3 * 4 + leaf lane 2. The resident man's B *is* the stored value — 0 until the first WRITE, so there is no initialisation pass. READ 12 ticks, WRITE 8.

regions.name: cell addr 15
regions.note: address 15 = mid lane 3 * 4 + leaf lane 3. The resident man's B *is* the stored value — 0 until the first WRITE, so there is no initialisation pass. READ 12 ticks, WRITE 8.

regions.name: collector block 3
regions.note: `R` takes whichever pipe is ready — this block's 4 cells, plus the chain from the block above — and `s` forwards it south. No pipe affinity needed, which is why the answer path is a chain beside the cells rather than 16 long pipes converging on one room.

circles.name: `/` address split
circles.note: `>rM4W/bW`: A=addr, B=4, then `/` leaves quotient in A and remainder in B in one glyph; `b` loads BP=quotient and `W` brings the remainder back to A for the lane's `s`. addr = block*4 + local.
